             ``dry_run`` is not. Must equal exactly
             ``remove-project <project>`` (byte-for-byte -- no trimming,
             no case-folding). A missing or wrong value is refused 422
             before any subprocess is spawned. Ignored when ``force`` is
             not True: the safe mode needs no confirmation.

             neither ``force`` nor ``confirm`` is required for a preview.

get.description:
Return per-agent average wall time, tokens and tasks, and total tokens
and tasks, over a span of shipped RCs for one project.

The REST twin of ``team/scripts/dashboard/agent-metrics.sh``: both
surfaces select the span with ``select_rc_span()``, compute with
``compute_agent_averages()`` and round every average with
``round_one_decimal()``, all from ``pgai_agent_kanban.lib.agent_metrics``
(the CLI's own ``team/scripts/lib/agent_metrics.py`` imports the same
functions rather than defining copies), over the per-RC metrics rollups
under ``projects/<name>/metrics/rc/v*.json``. This handler never
re-derives the span, averaging or rounding arithmetic. Only rollups whose
own ``outcome`` is ``shipped`` enter any figure; readable non-shipped
rollups inside the span are counted in ``excluded_count``. Thousands
separation is a presentation concern the CLI's renderer alone applies --
every number here is a plain JSON number.

Query parameters:

- ``project`` (required) — project name. No registration check against
  ``projects.cfg`` is performed -- this exactly matches the CLI twin's
  own ``--project`` handling, which accepts any name and renders the
  "no metrics yet" placeholder (here: an empty ``agents`` array) when
  the project has no ``metrics/rc/`` directory, whether because the
  name is unregistered or because the project has not shipped an RC
  yet. Missing entirely returns 422.
- ``window`` (optional, int) — the newest N shipped RCs (default: 10,
  the CLI's own ``--window`` default). A non-positive value returns 422.
- ``last`` (optional, int) — the newest N shipped RCs; the same span as
  ``window`` (the CLI's ``--last N``). A non-positive value returns 422.
- ``all`` (optional, bool) — when true, every shipped RC (the CLI's
  ``--all``). ``all=false`` selects nothing and is the same as omitting it.
- ``since`` (optional, str) — every shipped RC at or above ``vX.Y.Z`` by
  semantic-version order (the CLI's ``--since vX.Y.Z``; the leading
  ``v`` is optional). A value that is not a version returns 422.

At most one of ``window``, ``last``, ``all=true`` and ``since`` may be
given -- the CLI's span flags are mutually exclusive the same way; two
or more return 422 naming them. ``window`` counts as given only when it
appears in the query string.

Response body (HTTP 200):
  ``{"project": str, "window": int,
     "span": {"kind": "last"|"all"|"since",
              "count": int|null, "since": str|null},
     "shipped_count": int, "excluded_count": int,
     "agents": [{"agent": str, "avg_wall_minutes": float|null,
                  "avg_tokens": float, "avg_tasks": float,
                  "rc_count": int, "total_tokens": int,
                  "total_tasks": int},
                 ...],
     "warnings": [...]}``

  ``window`` is the span's RC bound: N for a ``window``/``last`` span
  (10 by default), and ``shipped_count`` for an ``all`` or ``since``
  span. ``span`` names the selected span: ``kind`` is ``last`` with
  ``count`` N, ``all``, or ``since`` with ``since`` the version bound
  as given; the unused member is ``null``. ``shipped_count`` is the
  number of shipped RCs the span selected (it can be below N when
  fewer have shipped) and ``excluded_count`` the number of non-shipped
  rollups inside the span's range -- the two numbers the CLI's footer
  narrates ("window: 5 shipped RCs (1 cancelled excluded)").

  ``agents`` is sorted by agent name ascending (matches the CLI
  renderer's own sort). An agent with zero invocations in the span is
  simply absent -- never a zero-average or a division-by-zero entry.
  ``avg_wall_minutes``, ``avg_tokens`` and ``avg_tasks`` carry exactly
  one decimal, rounded half away from zero by the shared one-decimal
  rule the CLI uses; ``total_tokens`` and ``total_tasks`` are raw
  integer sums over the agent's invocation RCs (``rc_count``).
  ``avg_wall_minutes`` is a mean PER TASK (a different denominator from
  ``avg_tokens``/``avg_tasks``, which are each a mean per invocation
  RC): it pools each invocation RC's own ``wall``.``by_agent`` entry
  for the agent and is ``null`` when none of those RCs carry one (the
  CLI renders that case as ``--``). ``agents`` is an empty list when
  the span holds no shipped rollup -- the same placeholder condition
  the CLI renders as "(no metrics yet)".

HTTP status:
  200 — success, including an empty ``agents`` array.
  422 — ``project`` is missing or empty; ``window`` or ``last`` is not
        a positive integer; ``since`` is not a vX.Y.Z version; or more
        than one of ``window``, ``last``, ``all=true`` and ``since`` is
        given.

get.summary: Per-agent, per-project averages and totals over a span of shipped RCs (CLI/REST parity)

get.description:
Return pending HUMAN-APPROVE gate tasks as a structured JSON array. Reads task state directly from the kanban filesystem — no shell-out. One implementation (collect_pending_approvals) backs both this endpoint and the window-14 dashboard renderer. Query parameters: - ``project`` (optional) — project name; when absent, all projects are aggregated (no default project, per house rule). When supplied and the project does not exist, returns 422. Response body (HTTP 200): ``[{"task_id": str, "project": str, "state": str, "rc": str, "target_version": str, "age": str, "review": str, "review_cmds": list[str], "approve_cmd": str, "reject_cmd": str}, ...]`` ``review_cmds`` is an ordered list of verbatim copy-paste-ready command strings: ``scripts/show.sh --project

--key `` always first; ``scripts/show-test-report.sh --project

--key `` appended when the target RC version is known (starts with "v"). Always non-empty. Returns an empty array ``[]`` when no approvals are pending. Note: the ``warnings`` dependency is wired (unknown query params are captured) but the warnings list is not yet surfaced in this response. Array-shaped responses cannot carry a top-level ``warnings`` key without a non-additive shape change; that ICD bump is tracked separately. HTTP status: 200 — success (including empty array). 422 — project parameter supplied but project does not exist.

200.description: JSON array of pending approval records (ICD 1.1.0); empty array on a clean system. Each record includes review_cmds (ordered list of copy-paste-ready review command strings), approve_cmd, and reject_cmd.

get.description:
Return OVERWATCH auto-resolution ledger entries as a structured JSON array.

Reads the append-only auto-resolutions ledger
(``projects/<name>/auto-resolutions.md``) directly from the kanban
filesystem — no shell-out. One implementation
(``collect_auto_resolutions`` in ``dashboard/scan_auto_resolutions.py``)
backs both this endpoint and the human-review tmux window's
Auto-Resolutions section, so the JSON body and the pane are guaranteed
to agree on which resolution events exist.

This surface is READ-ONLY: it never writes to the ledger and offers no
approve/reject/mutate affordance — the surface informs, it never
mutates state.

Query parameters:

- ``project`` (optional) — project name; when absent, all projects are
  aggregated (no default project, per house rule — same convention as
  ``GET /approvals``). When supplied and the project does not exist,
  returns 422.

Response body (HTTP 200):
  ``[{"project": str, "rc": str, "attempt_from": int|null,
      "attempt_to": int|null, "ceiling": str, "attempt_display": str,
      "decision": str, "outcome": str, "trigger": str,
      "findings": list[str], "evidence_paths": list[str],
      "ledger_path": str, "entry_id": str, "family_key": str|null,
      "timestamp": str}, ...]``

  ``attempt_display`` is the "N/M" string (``attempt_from`` over the
  project's configured retry ceiling); ``ceiling`` renders "?" when the
  retry-ceiling config cannot be resolved for that project (a read-only
  display degrades gracefully rather than raising — same convention as
  the tmux renderer). ``outcome`` is the backfilled terminal state
  (e.g. "SHIPPED attempt 2") or the literal string "pending" while the
  bundle family has not yet reached a terminal state. ``evidence_paths``
  and ``ledger_path``/``entry_id`` together form the drilldown to the
  TESTER report and the ledger entry that the Auto-Resolutions tab
  renders — the ledger is the index, not the record, so evidence paths
  point at the underlying reports rather than duplicating their content.

  Records are newest-first within each project; projects are ordered
  alphabetically (same ordering as the tmux renderer).

  Returns an empty array ``[]`` when no auto-resolutions have ever run.

HTTP status:
  200 — success (including empty array).
  422 — project parameter supplied but project does not exist.

200.description: JSON array of auto-resolution ledger records; empty array when no autonomous resolutions have ever run. Each record includes evidence_paths (TESTER report / HALT file / release-state links) and ledger_path + entry_id (the ledger entry link) — the drilldown pair the browser Auto-Resolutions tab renders.

get.description:
Return the unified kanban board aggregation view.

Returns all registered projects and all eight columns with structured items.
Status classification mirrors the tmux dashboard renderer exactly — see
board_classifier.py for the shared logic.

Column order (fixed): BUGS, PRIORITIES, REQUIREMENTS, PM, CODER, WRITER, TESTER, CM.

Item composite id format: ``<project>/<kind>/<key>``

Item status vocabulary: ``open | working | done | wont-do | blocked | label``
- ``label``   — requirements item targeting the currently active RC
- ``working`` — task in WORKING state (renderer calls this "running")
- ``blocked`` — task in BLOCKED state, or a quarantined intake file
- ``done``    — task in DONE state, or a shipped requirements item
- ``wont-do`` — task in WONT-DO state
- ``open``    — all other items

Per-column per-project item caps mirror the tmux renderer's
``dashboard_max_rows`` setting (from projects.cfg; default 20).
Items beyond the cap are counted in ``truncated``, not returned.

Quarantined files (in ``bugs/.rejected/`` and ``priority/.rejected/``)
surface as kind=quarantine items with status=blocked.

Query parameters:

- ``project`` (forbidden) — returns 422; the board is always unfiltered.

Response fields:

- ``generated_at``  — ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of this response.
- ``projects``      — list of registered projects with name, color, halt.
- ``columns``       — list of eight column objects (name, items, truncated).

HTTP status: 200 on success, 422 when ``?project=`` is supplied.

parameters.description: Not accepted. GET /board is the unfiltered aggregation view; the UI filters client-side.  Supplying this parameter returns 422.
parameters.name: project

schema.description: Not accepted. GET /board is the unfiltered aggregation view; the UI filters client-side.  Supplying this parameter returns 422.
schema.title: Project

200.description: JSON board with project list and eight columns (BUGS, PRIORITIES, REQUIREMENTS, PM, CODER, WRITER, TESTER, CM), each with structured item objects carrying composite ids, server-classified statuses, and per-column truncation counts.

get.description:
Return cost report data for the requested project and scope.

When ``format`` is omitted, delegates to ``cost-report.sh`` and returns the
standard text envelope.  The text output is byte-identical to the pre-v1.6.0
behavior.

When ``format=json`` is supplied, returns a JSON object with per-RC row
objects and the warnings list.  A ``project`` parameter is required for
``format=json``; omitting it returns 422.

- ``rc``    — single RC; the JSON array contains one row for that RC.
- ``month`` — all RC files whose shipped_at starts with ``YYYY-MM``.
- ``day``   — all RC files whose shipped_at starts with ``YYYY-MM-DD``.

- ``project`` (optional) — project name.
- ``month``   (optional) — calendar month ``YYYY-MM``.
- ``day``     (optional) — single day ``YYYY-MM-DD``.
- ``rc``      (optional) — RC version string (e.g. ``v1.2.0``).
- ``format``  (optional) — when ``json``, returns a JSON object instead of the
                           text envelope.

Text response envelope:
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "warnings": list[str]}``

JSON response (``?format=json``):
  ``[{"version": str, "tokens_in": int, "est_cost": float, ...}, ...]``

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout, and stderr from cost-report.sh; or a JSON array of per-RC row objects when ?format=json is supplied.

Return the rendered output for a named dashboard pane.

Accepted pane names (case-sensitive):

- ``queue``         — Calls ``column-render.sh queue`` (agent queue column).
- ``metrics``       — Calls ``dashboard/show-metrics.sh``.

Response envelope:
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "warnings": list[str]}``

HTTP status: 422 when an unknown pane is requested; otherwise 200/500 from
the underlying script.

get.description:
Return *project*'s DEEP-VERIFY ledger entries and current status.

The REST twin of the "deep-verify-status" read verb (team/scripts/
deep-verify-status.sh). Both surfaces resolve through the exact same
function, ``pgai_agent_kanban.ops.read.get_deep_verify_status``, which
delegates to ``pgai_agent_kanban.deep_verify.ledger`` for the ledger
data and to ``pgai_agent_kanban.deep_verify.schedule.resolve_mode`` for
THIS project's own configured cadence (project.cfg [release]
deep_verify) -- never the kanban-wide default, and never a route
fronting the "deep-verify" ACTION verb (POST /operations/deep-verify,
which runs the cold-build lane): this route only ever reads the
ledger, never runs anything and never writes a record.

Query parameters:

- ``project`` (required) — project name as registered in projects.cfg.

Response body (200):
  ``{"project": str, "mode": "weekly"|"off", "entries": [{"timestamp",
  "project", "version", "commit", "verdict", "detail"}, ...],
  "latest": {same shape}|null, "warnings": list[str]}``. ``entries`` is
  ``[]`` and ``latest`` is ``null`` when the project has never been
  deep-verified.

Response body on refusal (404 project not found, 422 malformed ledger
or unrecognized deep_verify config value):
  ``{"project": str, "error": str, "message": str, "remedy": str,
  "warnings": list[str]}``.

HTTP status:
  200 on success.
  404 when ``project`` does not resolve to a registered project.
  422 when the ledger is malformed or project.cfg [release]
  deep_verify holds a value outside its accepted vocabulary.

200.description: JSON body with project, mode, entries, latest, and warnings on success; project, error, message, remedy, and warnings on a refusal or a not-found project.

get.summary: A project's DEEP-VERIFY ledger entries and current status (read-only)

get.description:
Return service liveness information.

Response body fields:

- ``service``      — fixed string identifying this API service.
- ``kanban_root``  — resolved kanban root path (from PGAI_AGENT_KANBAN_ROOT_PATH).
- ``version``      — installed kanban version read from the VERSION file
                     on each request (same value as ``installed``; kept for
                     backward compatibility with existing consumers).
- ``installed``    — kanban version currently on disk (read from VERSION on each
                     request); reflects the most recent install.
- ``running``      — kanban version that was on disk when this server process
                     started; baked once at startup and never re-read.  An
                     orphaned server that survived a deploy will report its
                     true startup-time version here, allowing callers to detect
                     version skew between running code and installed code.
- ``warnings``     — always-present list; empty on a clean call; populated with
                     one entry per unknown query parameter supplied by the caller.

200.description: JSON object with service name, kanban root path, installed version, running version, and warnings list.

get.description:
Return the tail of a named log file.

Path parameter:

- ``kind`` — log kind selector.  One of: ``wake``, ``cm``, ``agent``,
             ``debug``, ``overwatch``, ``api-server``.
             Unknown kind → 404.

Query parameters (all optional unless noted):

- ``agent``   — required for ``wake``, ``agent``, ``debug`` kinds.
                Must be one of the fixed agent-role names:
                pm, po, coder, writer, tester, cm, overwatch.
                Traversal sequences → 422 before any file access.
- ``project`` — required for ``agent``, ``debug`` kinds.
                Must match a name in the project registry.
                For ``overwatch``, accepts a registered project name or
                the literal ``global`` for the global overwatch log.
                Traversal sequences → 422 before any file access.
- ``tail``    — number of lines to return from the end of the file.
                Default: 200.  Hard cap: 2000 (values above are clamped).
                ``tail == 0`` or negative → 422.

Response envelope (HTTP 200 on success):

- ``exit_code`` — 0 when the file was found and read; 1 when not found.
- ``stdout``    — the tail text (empty when exit_code is 1).
- ``stderr``    — error description when exit_code is 1; empty otherwise.
- ``warnings``  — always-present list; one entry per unknown query parameter.

HTTP status:

- 200  — successful response (file found or not; see exit_code).
- 404  — unknown kind value.
- 422  — validation failure (missing param, traversal, invalid agent/project,
          invalid tail value).

Path confinement:

The (kind, params) tuple is mapped to a KNOWN path via a server-side table.
No client-supplied string is concatenated into a filesystem path without first
being validated against a whitelist.  Traversal attempts return 422 before
any filesystem access.

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout (tail text), and stderr.

get.description:
Return historical RC metrics for the requested project(s).

When ``format`` is omitted, delegates to ``dashboard/show-metrics.sh`` and
returns the standard text envelope.  The text output is byte-identical to
the pre-v1.6.0 behavior.

When ``format=json`` is supplied and ``project`` is specified, returns a JSON
array of per-RC row objects read from the same ``metrics/history.csv`` that
the text renderer uses (sibling rule: one source, two formats).  A ``project``
parameter is required for ``format=json``; omitting it returns 422.

Query parameters:

- ``project``   (optional) — project name; omit to iterate all projects (text only).
- ``last``      (optional, int) — show last N rows (default: 10).
- ``per_agent`` (optional, bool) — when true, passes ``--per_agent`` to the text
                renderer; per-agent breakdown for the most recent RC.
                Not applicable for ``format=json``.
- ``format``    (optional) — when ``json``, returns a JSON array of row objects
                instead of the text envelope.

Text response envelope:
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "warnings": list[str]}``

JSON response (``?format=json``):
  ``[{"version": str, "tasks": int, "wall_seconds": float, "blocked_seconds": float, "tokens_in": int, ...}, ...]``
  Fields present only when the underlying source has a non-empty value.
  ``blocked_seconds`` is the row's ``history.csv`` ``blocked_minutes``
  column converted to seconds -- the same figure the text renderer's
  "Blocked" column shows, resolved through
  ``pgai_agent_kanban.metrics.blocked_ledger.blocked_minutes()`` at
  RC-close time, never recomputed here from task folders.
  Note: this array response does not carry a top-level ``warnings`` key;
  adding one requires a non-additive shape change tracked separately.

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout, and stderr from dashboard/show-metrics.sh; or a JSON array of per-RC row objects (including blocked_seconds, the REST twin of the text renderer's Blocked column) when ?format=json is supplied.

post.description:
Register an existing project directory in projects.cfg.

Thin passthrough to add-project.sh.  The project directory must already
exist; add-project.sh does not create anything on disk — it only updates
the registry.  Script guards (directory not found, already registered)
propagate unchanged in the envelope as non-zero exit_code.

Body fields:

- ``project``    (required) — project name.
- ``priority``   (optional, int) — registry priority (next available if absent).
- ``color``      (optional) — registry display color (e.g. ``'#RRGGBB'``).
- ``no_migrate`` (optional, bool) — when True, suppresses projects.cfg migration.
- ``dry_run``    (optional, bool) — when True, returns the planned action description
                                     without mutating registry.

Response envelope (exit_code 0):
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "warnings": list}``

Response on a refused call:
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "error": str,
  "message": str, "remedy": str, "warnings": list}`` at 500 when the
  script exited non-zero -- its own dual-channel triple lifted out of
  ``stderr`` as top-level keys, or its plain stderr text as ``message``
  under the stable fallback key ``add_project.refused`` with a runnable
  CLI remedy (``_make_dual_channel_envelope``);
  ``{"error": "add_project.<field>_required", "message": str, "remedy": str,
  "warnings": list}`` at 422 when this layer refused a body missing a
  required field, before any subprocess runs -- never the framework's
  ``{"detail": [...]}`` list.

HTTP status: 200 on exit_code 0, 500 on non-zero, 422 on validation failure.

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout, and stderr from add-project.sh.

post.description:
Cleanly abandon an in-flight RC: delete its branch, reset release-state.md.

The REST twin of the ``cancel-rc`` verb (``scripts/cm/cancel-rc.sh``).
Everything the script decides -- version format, current-branch check,
Active-RC match, idempotent no-op when already cancelled -- is the
script's own and propagates unchanged: the script refuses with plain
stderr lines (no house-shape block), so on a non-zero exit that text is
returned as ``message`` under the stable key ``cancel_rc.refused`` with
``stdout``/``stderr`` still carried in full.

The one API-layer gate is the confirmation. The CLI asks "Proceed?"
interactively unless ``--yes`` is given; an HTTP request has no
terminal to answer, so the body's ``yes`` field is that answer. When
``dry_run`` is not True, ``yes`` must be True or the route refuses 422
before the script is invoked -- the same explicit-opt-in shape
``POST /operations/remove-project`` applies to ``force``. The API is
not gentler than the CLI: the CLI would have stopped at the prompt.

Body fields:

- ``project`` (required) — project name. Passed as ``--project``.
- ``key``     (required) — RC version to cancel (``vX.Y.Z``). Passed as
               ``--key``; its format is checked by the script, not here.
- ``yes``     (required unless ``dry_run`` is true) — passes ``--yes``;
               the confirmation an HTTP caller cannot give interactively.
- ``dry_run`` (optional, bool) — when True, returns the planned action
               description without spawning anything; ``yes`` is not
               required for a preview.

Response envelope (exit_code 0):
  ``{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "warnings": list}``

Response on a refused call:
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "error": str,
  "message": str, "remedy": str, "warnings": list}`` at 500 when the
  script refused; ``{"error": str, "message": str, "remedy": str,
  "warnings": list}`` at 422 when this layer refused (missing
  ``project``/``key``, or ``yes`` not given).

HTTP status: 200 on exit_code 0, 500 on non-zero, 422 on an API-layer
refusal.

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout, and stderr from cm/cancel-rc.sh; on a refused call the body also carries error, message and remedy.

Close or resolve a task or intake item.

  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "error": str,

post.description:
Start the cold-build lane for a project, outside any RC.

The REST twin of the ``cold-build-now`` verb. cold-build-now.sh is a
named alias that execs ``deep-verify.sh --project NAME`` -- same flag,
same work, same exit codes -- so this route takes exactly the detached
path ``POST /operations/deep-verify`` takes (module docstring, "Long-
running verbs"): the script is launched with ``_spawn_detached`` and
the handler returns as soon as the child starts. The response confirms
the run STARTED; it never reports a verdict. Poll the project's
deep-verify ledger, ``GET /deep-verify-status``, or ``GET /verdicts``
once the backgrounded run completes. A refusal the script raises after
dispatch (an unregistered project, say) lands in the captured log file
the response names and in the ledger -- it cannot be carried in this
response, exactly as for deep-verify.

Body fields:

- ``project`` (required) — project whose ledger the run is filed under.
- ``image``   (optional, list of names or ``"all"``) — the container
               images this call builds, from
               team/config/container-images.txt; one ``--image <entry>``
               per entry, in order, which cold-build-now.sh passes on to
               deep-verify.sh. Omitted: no ``--image``, so kanban.cfg
               [release] container_images applies, else the script lists
               the images and builds nothing. See the module docstring's
               "Container image selection" note.
- ``dry_run`` (optional, bool) — when True, returns the planned action
               description; no subprocess (detached or otherwise) is
               started.

Response envelope (real invocation):
  ``{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "cold-build-now: started ...", "stderr": "", "warnings": list}``

Response on a refused call (422, missing ``project``):
  ``{"error": "cold_build_now.project_required", "message": str, "remedy": str, "warnings": list}``

Response on a refused call (422, ``image`` names an undeclared image):
  ``{"error": "container_tier.unknown_image", "message": str, "remedy": str, "warnings": list}``

HTTP status: 200 once the detached run has started (dispatch success,
NOT a verdict); 422 when ``project`` is missing or empty, or when
``image`` names an image the manifest does not declare (both refused
before anything is spawned, ``dry_run`` included). A start failure
(e.g. the script is not executable) raises rather than returning a
fabricated envelope.

200.description: JSON envelope confirming the backgrounded run started; NEVER a verdict. On a refused call the body carries error, message and remedy.

post.description:
Start the DEEP-VERIFY tier's on-demand run for a project.

Unlike every other operation in this router, a real (non-dry-run) call
does NOT wait for the underlying script to finish: deep-verify.sh itself
blocks for the duration of the cold-build lane (budget ~13 minutes), and
holding an HTTP connection open that long is the exact case this endpoint
exists to avoid. The script is launched detached
(see ``_spawn_detached`` above) and this handler returns as soon as the
child process starts. The response confirms the run STARTED; it never
reports a verdict, because the lane has not produced one yet. Poll the
project's deep-verify ledger (``$KANBAN_ROOT/projects/<name>/deep-verify-
ledger.md``) or ``GET /verdicts`` once the backgrounded run completes.

Body fields:

- ``project``   (required unless ``scheduled`` is true with no project —
                 the scheduled fan-out mode) — project whose ledger the
                 run is filed under.
- ``scheduled`` (optional, bool) — passed as ``--scheduled``; self-gates
                 on the project's ledger age and off-hours window.
- ``image``     (optional, list of names or ``"all"``) — the container
                 images this call builds, from
                 team/config/container-images.txt; one ``--image <entry>``
                 per entry, in order. Omitted: no ``--image``, so
                 kanban.cfg [release] container_images applies, else the
                 script lists the images and builds nothing. See the
                 module docstring's "Container image selection" note.
- ``dry_run``   (optional, bool) — when True, returns the planned action
                 description; no subprocess (detached or otherwise) is
                 started.

Response envelope (real invocation):
  ``{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "deep-verify: started ...", "stderr": "", "warnings": list}``

Response on a refused call (422, ``project`` missing and ``scheduled`` not true):
  ``{"error": "deep_verify.project_required", "message": str, "remedy": str, "warnings": list}``

Response on a refused call (422, ``image`` names an undeclared image):
  ``{"error": "container_tier.unknown_image", "message": str, "remedy": str, "warnings": list}``

HTTP status: 200 once the detached run has started (dispatch success, NOT
a verdict), 422 when ``project`` is missing and ``scheduled`` is not true
or when ``image`` names an image the manifest does not declare (both
refused before anything is spawned, ``dry_run`` included).
A start failure (e.g. the script is not executable) raises rather than
returning a fabricated envelope — there is no completed subprocess to
report exit_code/stdout/stderr from.

200.description: JSON envelope confirming the backgrounded run started; NEVER a verdict.

post.description:
Unwind an in-flight release candidate across all state stores.

Every call that runs the script is a confirmed one. unwind-rc.sh asks
"Type 'yes' to continue" before touching anything; the adapter runs it
with stdin closed, so an unanswered prompt reads EOF and aborts. The
body's ``confirm`` string is the answer: when it equals exactly
``unwind-rc <project> <key>`` (byte-for-byte -- no trimming, no
case-folding) the route passes ``--confirm`` and the script runs
non-interactively; a missing or wrong string is refused 422 here, before
any subprocess is spawned. ``force`` is a separate escalation that
passes ``--force`` and bypasses ONLY the script's Active-RC
version-mismatch check -- it still needs ``confirm``, so no call can
skip a guard without also having been confirmed.

Pre-flight guards enforced by unwind-rc.sh propagate unchanged in the envelope:

- HALT must be set (per-project or global) before unwinding.
- Active RC in release-state.md must match ``key`` (bypassable with ``force``).

These guards surface as non-zero exit_code and populated stderr, mapped to HTTP 500.

Body fields:

- ``project`` (required) — project name.
- ``key``     (required) — RC version to unwind (e.g. ``v1.2.0``).
- ``confirm`` (required unless ``dry_run`` is true) — must equal exactly
              ``unwind-rc <project> <key>``. Any mismatch → 422 naming
              ``confirm``, no subprocess spawned.
- ``force``   (optional, bool) — when True, passes ``--force`` (bypass Active-RC version
                                 mismatch check; does NOT bypass HALT or other guards,
                                 and does NOT stand in for ``confirm``).
- ``dry_run`` (optional, bool) — when True, returns the argv a live call would run
                                  without spawning anything; the script never receives
                                  ``--dry-run`` from this route. ``confirm`` is not
                                  required for a preview.

Response envelope (exit_code 0):
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "warnings": list}``

Response on a refused call:
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "error": str,
  "message": str, "remedy": str, "warnings": list}`` at 500 when the
  script exited non-zero -- its own dual-channel triple lifted out of
  ``stderr`` as top-level keys, or its plain stderr text as ``message``
  under the stable fallback key ``unwind_rc.refused`` with a runnable
  CLI remedy (``_make_dual_channel_envelope``);
  ``{"error": "unwind_rc.<field>_required", "message": str, "remedy": str,
  "warnings": list}`` at 422 when this layer refused a body missing a
  required field, or ``{"error": "unwind_rc.confirm_mismatch", ...}``
  when ``confirm`` is present but wrong -- before any subprocess runs,
  never the framework's ``{"detail": [...]}`` list.

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout, and stderr from unwind-rc.sh.

post.summary: Fully unwind an in-flight release candidate

post.description:
Fire one or all pipeline agents' wake cycle outside their cron cadence.

Delegates to wake-now.sh -- the mutual-exclusivity refusal between
``agent`` and ``all``, and the "one of them is required" refusal when
neither is supplied, are the script's own guards and propagate unchanged
in the envelope's foreground path rather than being re-implemented here.

See the module docstring's "Long-running verbs" note for WHY ``bg``/
``all`` take a different dispatch path than every other endpoint in this
router: wake-now.sh's own backgrounding (a bare ``&``) inherits
shell_out()'s capture pipes instead of closing them, so a plain
shell_out() call on ``bg``/``all`` would silently block for the fired
agent's ENTIRE wake cycle -- exactly the many-minutes-blocking case this
ticket exists to avoid. ``bg``/``all`` therefore launch wake-now.sh
detached (like POST /operations/deep-verify) and return as soon as the
fork completes; the response confirms wake-now.sh STARTED, not that any
fired agent finished. Supplying neither ``bg`` nor ``all`` uses the
normal blocking shell_out() dispatch -- wake-now.sh execs wake-batch.sh
directly in that mode (no background job, no pipe-inheritance hazard),
so this is a faithful, non-gentler mirror of the bare CLI's own
foreground contract.

Body fields:

- ``agent``   (required unless ``all`` is true) — agent role to wake
              (``pm``, ``coder``, ``cm``, ``writer``, ``tester``,
              ``overwatch``).
- ``all``     (optional, bool) — fire every pipeline agent. Detached path.
- ``bg``      (optional, bool) — background the single named agent's wake
              cycle. Detached path. Recommended for HTTP callers over
              foreground mode.
- ``dry_run`` (optional, bool) — when True, returns the planned action
              description without firing anything (checked before ``bg``/
              ``all`` route to the detached path).

Response envelope:
  - Detached path (``bg`` or ``all``): ``{"exit_code": 0, "stdout":
    "wake-now: started ...", "stderr": "", "warnings": list}`` — always
    200, confirming dispatch started, never that the fired agent(s)
    finished.
  - Foreground path (neither ``bg`` nor ``all``): the normal envelope
    with wake-now.sh's own completed exit_code/stdout/stderr.

HTTP status: 200 on the detached path or on foreground exit_code 0, 500
on a non-zero foreground exit_code (including wake-now.sh's own
agent/all guards).

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout, and stderr from wake-now.sh.

Return a task's README.md content, byte-identical to show-readme.sh.

Path parameters:

- ``project`` (required) — project name.
- ``key``     (required) — task key.  Prefix resolution is supported,
                           matching show.sh / show-readme.sh (an
                           agent+date+seq prefix suffices when it
                           resolves unambiguously).

Response envelope (HTTP 200 on success):
  ``{"exit_code": 0, "stdout": "<README.md content>", "stderr": "", "warnings": [...]}``

HTTP status:

- 200 — the key resolved to a task and its README.md was found; ``stdout``
        carries the file content verbatim (byte-identical to
        ``show-readme.sh --project <project> --key <key>``).
- 404 — no README resource exists at this (project, key): the key is not
        found, the key resolves to a ledger item (bug/priority/requirement
        — READMEs are task artifacts only, same refusal show-readme.sh
        applies), or the task directory has no README.md file.  The body
        carries ``{"error": "task readme not found", "project", "key",
        "detail"}`` with show-readme.sh's stderr message in ``detail``.
- 422 — ``project`` or ``key`` contains a path-traversal sequence (``..``,
        ``/``, ``\\``, or their URL-encoded forms).  Returned before any
        subprocess is spawned or any file is opened.

Security — path confinement:

show-readme.sh resolves ``key`` via the same resolver used by show.sh,
close.sh, and friends; that resolver concatenates the raw key into
filesystem paths with no traversal sanitisation of its own.  This handler
is therefore the confinement gate: ``project`` and ``key`` are checked for
traversal sequences (raw and URL-encoded) BEFORE show-readme.sh is
invoked — no user-supplied string is concatenated into a filesystem path
by this handler, and a traversal-shaped value in either parameter is
rejected before any subprocess is spawned.  This mirrors the discipline
the logs and traces routers apply to their own query parameters.

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout (README.md content), and stderr from show-readme.sh.

renders ``get_queues``' result through
``pgai_agent_kanban.dashboard.queue_pane`` -- the renderer the CLI uses
-- so ``stdout`` is the pane show-queues.sh prints (colour follows the
server's ``TERM``/``NO_COLOR``; with no ``project`` the counters come

``queue_details.resolve_queue_details`` structure the CLI's
``--details`` listing renders -- as JSON rather than coloured text.

- ``project`` (optional) — project to render.

  - ``details=true``: a single project's shape when given; every
    registered project, nested by name, when omitted (iterate-all,
    matching the CLI's own ``--details`` behavior with no ``--project``).

  instead of the compact one-line-per-agent summary.

every REST invocation renders against the server's own configured kanban
root, never a caller-supplied path.

(``show_queues.project_directory_missing``), or when ``project`` is
omitted and the server has no ``PGAI_PROJECT_NAME``
(``show_queues.no_project``). ``details=true``: 404 when
an explicit ``project`` does not resolve to a registered project.

Query parameters (all optional):

- ``project`` — filter by project name; absent = all projects.
                Traversal sequences → 422 before any filesystem access.
- ``agent``   — filter by agent role.  Must be one of the fixed agent-role
                names when provided: pm, po, coder, writer, tester, cm,
                overwatch.  Traversal sequences → 422.
- ``limit``   — maximum number of entries to return.  Default: 50.
                Hard cap: 2000 (values above are clamped).
                ``limit == 0`` or negative → 422.

Response: JSON array of trace objects, newest-first::

  [
    {
      "id":            "<opaque server-minted id>",
      "project":       "<project name>",
      "agent":         "<agent role>",
      "task_key":      "<TASK-KEY from filename>",
      "timestamp":     "<ISO-8601 timestamp from filename>",
      "path_basename": "<filename.md>"
    },
    ...
  ]

HTTP status:

- 200 — always (empty array when no traces match the filters).
- 422 — traversal sequence in project or agent param; invalid limit;
        agent value not in the fixed agent-role set.

Security:

get.description:
Return every registered project's lane verdict as JSON.

Resolved through ``verdict_resolve_project`` (``team/scripts/lib/verdict.sh``)
-- the exact function ``why.sh``'s CLI verdict line calls. This handler
never shells out to ``why.sh`` and never parses its rendered sentence,
and it never re-derives a verdict from project state itself: it shells
out to ``scripts/verdict-report.sh``, a thin sibling of ``why.sh`` that
formats the SAME resolved fields as machine-readable ``key=value``
blocks instead of prose, and this handler parses that structured
contract only.

``details=true`` extends this same parity guarantee to why.sh's full
``--details`` diagnostic pane -- release locks, queue tails, and the
resolved posture. Every extra field is resolved by ``verdict-report.sh``
through the SAME functions ``why.sh --details``' text renderers call
(``team/scripts/lib/lock_provenance.sh``, ``team/scripts/lib/
defer_posture.sh``'s ``resolve_defer_posture``, ``why_details.sh``'s own
HALT/HALT-AFTER helper, and ``team/scripts/lib/discovery_bundle.sh`` /
``discovery_state.sh``'s pending-bundle readers); this handler only
groups and reformats already-resolved ``kind=``-tagged blocks
(``_release_locks_from_detail_blocks``, ``_queue_tails_from_detail_
blocks``, ``_posture_from_detail_blocks``) into JSON, never a second
derivation of lock provenance, queue state, or deferral posture.

Query parameters:

- ``project`` (optional) — project name; when absent, every project
  registered in ``projects.cfg`` is returned, in the same priority
  order ``why.sh`` (no ``--project``) walks them. When supplied and the
  name is not registered in ``projects.cfg`` at all, returns 422. When
  supplied and the name IS registered but its ``projects/<name>``
  directory does not exist on disk, returns 200 with a single
  "unresolved" entry (see below) — a known registry entry with a
  missing directory is a diagnostic condition, not an unknown name.
- ``details`` (optional, bool) — when true, adds ``posture``,
  ``release_locks``, and ``queue_tails`` to the response (see below).
  Requires ``project`` — a posture/lock/queue report is always
  per-project, exactly like ``why.sh --project NAME --details`` itself
  requires ``--project``; omitting it returns 422.

Response body (HTTP 200, ``details`` absent or false):
  ``{"verdicts": [...], "warnings": [...]}``

Response body (HTTP 200, ``details=true``, project resolved):
  ``{"verdicts": [...], "posture": {...}, "release_locks": [...],
     "queue_tails": [...], "warnings": [...]}``. ``posture``,
  ``release_locks``, and ``queue_tails`` are omitted when the named
  project is "unresolved" (registered but no directory on disk) — there
  is nothing to detail for a project with no directory, matching
  ``why.sh --details``' own refusal for that case.

  ``posture`` — ``{"halt_state": "normal"|"halted"|"draining",
  "halt_event": str (present only when halt_state is not "normal" and
  an event was recorded), "deferred_bugs": {"value": str, "tier": str},
  "deferred_bug_level": {"value": str, "tier": str}, "defer_piggyback":
  {"value": str, "tier": str}, "until": {"value": str, "tier": str,
  "campaign_file": str (present only when tier is "campaign file")},
  "active_rc": "none"|"vX.Y.Z", "pending_bundles": [{"name": str,
  "status": str}, ...]}``.

  ``release_locks`` — one entry per lock held for the project:
  ``{"path": str, "age_seconds": int, "held_seconds": int|null,
  "provenance": str, "stale_threshold_seconds": int,
  "stale_threshold_derivation": str, "violation": bool}``. Empty when
  the project holds no locks. ``held_seconds`` is how long the lock
  has been held, computed from the lock record's ``acquired_at`` (the
  same value ``why.sh --details`` renders as ``held: <duration>``);
  it is ``null`` when the record carries no ``acquired_at`` (a
  pre-upgrade lock: "acquired_at not recorded"). ``age_seconds`` is
  the seconds since the lock file was last refreshed (its mtime) — a
  heartbeat age the held-lock refresh keeps resetting, not how long
  the lock has been held.

  ``queue_tails`` — one entry per ``tasks/queues/*_backlog.md`` file:
  ``{"agent": str, "entries": [{"marker": str, "task_id": str,
  "status_state": str}, ...]}``. ``entries`` is empty for a queue file
  with no matching lines. Empty overall when the project has no
  ``tasks/queues/`` directory at all.

Each entry in ``verdicts`` is one of two shapes:

  Resolved (the project directory exists and a verdict was reached):
    ``{"project": str, "verdict": "RUNNING"|"BLOCKED"|"HALTED"|"STUCK-LOCK"|"IDLE",
    "exit_code": int, "cause": str, "remedy": str, "line": str,
    "task_id": str, "task_state": str, "minutes_in_state": int}``.
    ``task_id``/``task_state`` are present only for RUNNING and BLOCKED
    (the only two verdicts naming an active task); ``minutes_in_state``
    is present only for RUNNING. A field with no content for a given
    project is omitted — never null or zero-filled. STALLED is not a
    distinct verdict word: a RUNNING task past the stall threshold keeps
    ``verdict: "RUNNING"`` with ``exit_code: 3`` (see
    ``team/scripts/lib/verdict.sh``) — this same entry shape is the
    "stall verdict" data ``details=true`` adds no separate field for.

  Unresolved (the project is registered in ``projects.cfg`` but has no
  directory on disk — a diagnostic condition distinct from any of the
  five verdict words; never silently reported as a false IDLE, which is
  what an empty task scan against a nonexistent directory would read
  as):
    ``{"project": str, "error": "project directory not found",
    "cause": str, "remedy": str}``.

HTTP status:
  200 — success, including when individual entries are "unresolved".
  422 — ``?project=`` names a value that is not registered in
        ``projects.cfg`` at all, or ``?details=true`` is given without
        ``?project=``.
  500 — ``verdict-report.sh`` exited non-zero for a reason other than
        an unresolved project directory (a genuine resolver failure).

Security: every string in the response is composed from project names,
task ids/states read from status.md, minute counts, and the resolver's
own cause/remedy sentences — no credential, token, or absolute path
outside the kanban root is ever included. A HALT-file path named in a
HALTED entry's cause/line is inside the kanban root — the same path
why.sh's own CLI line already prints.

200.description: JSON object with a 'verdicts' array (one entry per registered project, in projects.cfg priority order) and a 'warnings' array. Every entry is resolved through the same verdict engine (team/scripts/lib/verdict.sh) that team/scripts/why.sh's CLI verdict line calls -- the CLI and this endpoint can never disagree about what a lane's verdict is.

get.description:
Return the output of ``verify-rc-state.sh <project> [--verbose]``.

The REST twin of the "verify-rc-state" operator verb. Unlike every other
read verb this API fronts, the underlying script takes its project as a
REQUIRED POSITIONAL argument rather than a ``--project`` flag (see the
script's own header) -- this handler builds that positional argv
directly rather than routing through the shared ``shell_out``/
``build_argv`` flag-marshalling helper, which only knows how to emit
``--flag`` pairs. The script itself is invoked unchanged; no check
result is re-derived in Python.

Query parameters:

- ``project`` (required) — project name; mapped to the script's
  positional ``<project>`` argument.
- ``verbose`` (optional, bool) — when true, passes ``--verbose`` to print
  every check (OK, WARN, ERROR); by default only WARN/ERROR and the
  final summary line are printed, matching the CLI's own default.

Response envelope:
  ``{"exit_code": int, "stdout": str, "stderr": str, "warnings": list[str]}``

HTTP status:
  200 on exit_code 0 (no ERROR findings).
  500 on any non-zero exit_code -- both the script's own "1 error
  findings" and "2 pre-flight failure" outcomes map to 500, matching
  every other read endpoint's uniform exit-code-to-status contract in
  this file (see the module docstring's HTTP status mapping).
  422 when ``project`` is missing or empty.

200.description: JSON envelope with exit_code, stdout, and stderr from verify-rc-state.sh.

get.summary: Read-only consistency checker for a project's RC state
